title: 由“同相”和“两表读数相等”反推电路参数
statement: V_s = 100 V（有效值），ω = 1000 rad/s，L = 10 mH，R、C 未知。实验测得：电流表 A_1、A_2 读数相等，且电源电压 v_s 与总电流 i 同相。
以 V̇_s = 100∠0° V 为参考，用相量图求总电流 I、a 点电压 V_a、电流表读数以及 R、C 的值。

questions.explain: 相量图是等腰直角三角形：V̇_L ⊥ V̇_s 且 V_L = V_s = 100 V，所以 I = V_L/X_L = 100/10 = 10 A。

questions.ask: a 点电压 V_a（R、C 两端）= ?
questions.explain: V̇_a 是直角三角形的斜边：V_a = √(V_s² + V_L²) = 100√2 ≈ 141.4 V，相位 −45°。

questions.ask: 电流表 A_1 的读数 = ?
questions.explain: İ_R 与 V̇_a 同相，İ_C 超前 V̇_a 90°，两者等长，合成 İ 与 V̇_a 成 45°：I_R = I_C = I/√2 = 7.071 A。
X_C = V_a/I_C = 20 Ω，C = 1/(ωX_C) = 1/(1000 × 20) = 50 µF。验算：Z = j10 + 20∥(−j20) = j10 + (10 − j10) = 10 Ω，纯电阻，与“同相”一致——前面 I = 10 A 一问正是用这组 R、C 算出来的。

hints: 以并联部分的电压 V̇_a 为参考相量画图：İ_R 与 V̇_a 同相，İ_C 超前 90°，两者等长，所以 İ 超前 V̇_a 45°。
V̇_L = jX_L·İ 超前 İ 90°；而 V̇_s 与 İ 同相，所以 V̇_L ⊥ V̇_s。
KVL：V̇_a = V̇_s − V̇_L，三个电压构成一个直角三角形，再利用 45° 角。
solution: **1. 并联部分。** 设 V̇_a = V_a∠θ。I_R = I_C 且 İ_C 超前 İ_R 90°，所以 İ = İ_R + İ_C 的模 I = √2·I_R，且 İ 超前 V̇_a 45°。
**2. 同相条件。** v_s 与 i 同相，以 V̇_s = 100∠0° 为参考，则 İ = I∠0°，V̇_a = V_a∠−45°。

en.title: Recovering element values from “in phase” and “equal ammeter readings”
statement: V_s = 100 V (rms), ω = 1000 rad/s, L = 10 mH; R and C are unknown. Measurements show that ammeters A_1 and A_2 read the same, and that the source voltage v_s is in phase with the total current i.
Taking V̇_s = 100∠0° V as reference, use a phasor diagram to find the total current I, the voltage V_a at node a, the ammeter readings, and the values of R and C.

questions.explain: The phasor diagram is an isosceles right triangle: V̇_L ⊥ V̇_s and V_L = V_s = 100 V, so I = V_L/X_L = 100/10 = 10 A.

questions.ask: Voltage at node a, V_a (across R and C) = ?
questions.explain: V̇_a is the hypotenuse of the right triangle: V_a = √(V_s² + V_L²) = 100√2 ≈ 141.4 V, at −45°.
İ_R is in phase with V̇_a and İ_C leads V̇_a by 90°; with equal lengths their sum İ makes 45° with V̇_a: I_R = I_C = I/√2 = 7.071 A.

X_C = V_a/I_C = 20 Ω, C = 1/(ωX_C) = 1/(1000 × 20) = 50 µF. Check: Z = j10 + 20∥(−j20) = j10 + (10 − j10) = 10 Ω, purely resistive, consistent with "in phase" — the I = 10 A question above is computed with exactly these R and C.

hints: Draw the diagram with the parallel voltage V̇_a as reference: İ_R is in phase with V̇_a, İ_C leads by 90°, and they are equal, so İ leads V̇_a by 45°.
V̇_L = jX_L·İ leads İ by 90°, while V̇_s is in phase with İ, so V̇_L ⊥ V̇_s.
KVL: V̇_a = V̇_s − V̇_L; the three voltages form a right triangle — now use the 45° angle.
solution: **1. Parallel part.** Let V̇_a = V_a∠θ. Since I_R = I_C and İ_C leads İ_R by 90°, the sum İ = İ_R + İ_C has magnitude √2·I_R and leads V̇_a by 45°.
**2. In-phase condition.** v_s and i are in phase; with V̇_s = 100∠0° as reference, İ = I∠0° and V̇_a = V_a∠−45°.

**3. KVL and the phasor diagram.** V̇_s = V̇_L + V̇_a with V̇_L = jX_L·İ = 10I∠90°. So 100∠0° = j10I + V_a∠−45°: real part 100 = V_a cos45°, imaginary part 0 = 10I − V_a sin45°. Hence **V_a = 100√2 ≈ 141.4 V** and **I = 10 A** (V_L = 100 V, an isosceles right triangle).
**4. Ammeter readings.** I_R = I_C = I/√2 = **7.071 A**.
**5. Element values.** R = V_a/I_R = 20 Ω, X_C = V_a/I_C = 20 Ω → C = 1/(ωX_C) = **50 µF**; i.e. **R = 20 Ω, C = 50 µF**.
